items.stem: In Erlang, what happens when you match 1 = X where X is already bound to 2?

options.text: A pattern-match exception is raised because the values differ
options.rationale: Correct: = is a match operator, not assignment; an already-bound variable must match or it fails.
Erlang variables are single-assignment; they are never reassigned.
A failed match raises an exception rather than returning a boolean.
It compiles; the failure happens at run time when the match is evaluated.

items.explanation: Correct: = is a match operator, not assignment; an already-bound variable must match or it fails.

items.stem: Which statements about Erlang processes are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Processes communicate only by sending asynchronous messages
options.rationale: Correct: processes share no memory and exchange immutable messages.

options.text: Spawning a process is lightweight compared with an OS thread
options.rationale: Correct: BEAM processes are cheap, so systems commonly run many thousands.

options.text: Processes share a common mutable heap for speed
options.rationale: Each process has its own heap; there is no shared mutable memory.

options.text: A receive block can read another process's mailbox directly
options.rationale: A process can only read its own mailbox.

items.explanation: Correct: processes share no memory and exchange immutable messages.; Correct: BEAM processes are cheap, so systems commonly run many thousands.

items.stem: What is the main idea behind the 'let it crash' philosophy with OTP supervisors?

options.text: Let a faulty process fail fast and have a supervisor restart it into a known-good state
options.rationale: Correct: isolation plus supervised restart keeps the system healthy without defensive error handling everywhere.

options.text: Disable error logging so crashes are invisible
options.rationale: Crashes are logged; the point is recovery, not hiding faults.

options.text: Catch every possible exception inside the worker
options.rationale: That is the opposite of the philosophy, which avoids defensive over-handling.

options.text: Restart the entire node on any error
options.rationale: Supervisors restart the failed child, not usually the whole node.

items.explanation: Correct: isolation plus supervised restart keeps the system healthy without defensive error handling everywhere.
